newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-CALCAVECCHIA, RINKER SHARE HOPE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CALCAVECCHIA, RINKER SHARE HOPE LEAD.

text.p: Mark Calcavecchia shot a 67 to claim a share of the lead with Larry Rinker after the second round of the Bob Hope Classic golf tournament on Thursday.
Rinker, the first-round leader with a 63, shot a 68 on Thursday to share the lead at 13 under par.
Jay Don Blake was a stroke behind at 12 under after a 67, and Paul Goydos was one further back with a 68.

The Hope is played in a pro-am format over a rotation of four of the Coachella Valley's desert courses in the first four rounds. Rinker played at Indian Wells, the host course where all the pros will play for Sunday's final round.

Calcavecchia had his round at Indian Ridge on Thursday, as did Goydos. Blake played at Bermuda Dunes. La Quint, considered the most difficult of the four, accounted for just two scores among the top 10.

Rinker said the format of this tournament made it difficult to match his first-round, because "you're not playing the same course, where you can at least remember the good shots you hit the day before."
Rinker started with a birdie on the second hole, then three putted the fourth, the first of two bogeys. He had five additional birdies, including three in the last five holes.
Calcavecchia had one three-putt bogey and six birdies.

"I played well again," Calcavecchia said. "I gave myself a lot of good chances to make birdies, but missed three or four five footers. As Larry said, there's a long way to go. Everybody's spread out all over the place. You probably have to be in the mid 20's to win, so at 13 under par, I figure I'm halfway there."
